turns.content: In triangle ABC, BC=12 and angle B=30 degrees. Let AC=b and AC=c, and identify which side is opposite the given angle.
Apply the Law of Cosines to derive the quadratic equation for c. Use its discriminant to find when there are two distinct real values of c.
Use the sum and product of the roots of the same quadratic in BC, and determine when both possible values of AB are positive.
Examine the two boundary values of b: one makes the quadratic have a repeated root and the other makes one root zero. Decide whether either boundary gives two valid side lengths.
Check that every b strictly between those boundaries gives two positive roots that satisfy the triangle conditions.
Count the integer values of AC for which two distinct positive values of AB are possible.
